extracted.intended_audience: trademark applicants, trademark examining attorneys, and practitioners handling ex parte appeals to the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board (TTAB)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and evidentiary rules governing remand, suspension, publication, abandonment, cancellation, consolidation, and alternative positions in ex parte appeals to the TTAB, including required timeframes, filing obligations, and limitations on evidence and action by examining attorneys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board sua sponte remand (37 CFR § 2.142(f)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: If, during an appeal from a refusal of registration, it appears to the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board that an issue not previously raised may render the mark of the appellant unregistrable, the Board may suspend the appeal and remand the application to the examiner for further examination to be completed within thirty days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further examination must be completed within 30 days (or an extension). If the examining attorney, after consideration, does not believe the specified issue renders the mark unregistrable, the examiner must promptly return the application to the Board with a written statement that no additional requirement or ground resulted. If the further examination does result in an additional requirement or ground for refusal, the examiner and applicant proceed as specified in 37 CFR §§ 2.61–2.64; if the ground is made final the Board will allow 60 days to file a supplemental brief limited to the additional ground. See accompanying notes and cited cases (e.g., In re Opryland; In re Diet Tabs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on examining attorney upon remand (f(1) and f(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon remand under 37 CFR § 2.142(f)(1) or § 2.142(f)(6), the examining attorney may not make a requirement or refuse registration on a new ground not specified in the Board's remand letter (or in the examining attorney's request for remand).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examining attorney wishes to make a new requirement or refuse registration on a new ground not mentioned in the remand letter/request, the examining attorney must file a request with the Board for jurisdiction to make that new requirement or refusal. Nor may the examining attorney submit evidence relating to a requirement or ground not specified in the remand letter/request. See cited authorities (e.g., In re W.W. Henry Co.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental briefing and hearing procedure after remand yields additional ground
rubrics_metrics.description: If further examination on remand results in an additional ground for refusal that is made final, the Board will issue an order allowing the appellant sixty days from the date of the order to file a supplemental brief limited to the additional ground for the refusal of registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the supplemental brief is not filed within the allowed time (or extension), the appeal may be dismissed. If filed, the examining attorney shall, within 60 days after the supplemental brief is sent to the examiner, file a written brief answering it and mail a copy to the appellant; the appellant may file a reply brief within 20 days from date of mailing of the examiner's brief. If an oral hearing had been requested prior to remand but not yet held, it will be set and heard; if not previously requested or already held, an oral hearing may be requested by separate notice no later than ten days after the due date for a reply brief on the additional ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand upon request by examining attorney (37 CFR § 2.142(f)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: If, during an appeal from a refusal of registration, it appears to the examining attorney that an issue not involved in the appeal may render the mark unregistrable, the examining attorney may, by written request, ask the Board to suspend the appeal and remand the application to the examiner for further examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a request may be filed at any point prior to the Board's final decision, including when the examining attorney is to submit an appeal brief or supplemental brief. The Board will generally grant a valid request (the Office's mandate is to register only eligible marks). If granted, the Board will forward the application and allow a specified time in which the examining attorney must issue an Office action pursuant to the request; thereafter proceed as provided in 37 CFR §§ 2.61–2.64. The examining attorney may not make or rely on new grounds/evidence beyond the request (see limitations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter of protest procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A third party with knowledge of facts bearing upon registrability may file a 'letter of protest' with the Office of the Deputy Commissioner for Trademark Examination Policy, reciting the facts and accompanied by supporting evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Deputy Commissioner determines whether the information should be given to the examining attorney. Proceedings in an ex parte appeal are not suspended pending this determination. If a letter of protest is granted during an appeal and the examining attorney, after considering the supporting evidence, believes an issue not involved in the appeal may render the mark unregistrable, the examining attorney may file a written request with the Board pursuant to 37 CFR § 2.142(f)(6) to suspend the appeal and remand for further examination. See TMEP § 1715 and TBMP § 215.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant-requested remand vs. reconsideration (timing and good cause)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request filed by an applicant to remand the application to the examining attorney within six months of the issuance of a final Office action is treated as a request for reconsideration; requests filed more than six months after the final refusal (generally after filing the notice of appeal) are treated as requests for remand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for remand are generally filed to submit additional evidence or to amend the application, or to have the examiner consider a refusal in light of a recently decided case. A request for remand must include a showing of good cause; the Board will consider both the reason given and the point in the appeal at which the request is made. If the applicant has not filed its appeal brief prior to filing the request for remand, it should not file it until the Board acts on the remand request. If the request is granted, the Board will suspend proceedings and remand the application to the examining attorney; the Board’s order and directions will depend on the nature of the remand (see TBMP §§ 1207.02 and 1205.01 for examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval for publication (or registration) during appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The examining attorney may withdraw an appealed refusal to register and approve the involved application for publication (or for registration on the Supplemental Register) at any time prior to issuance of the Board's decision in the case, rendering the appeal moot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the examining attorney does so, the appeal becomes moot. The examining attorney should notify the applicant by telephone or e-mail that the application is being approved for publication or registration. See TMEP § 1501.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment during appeal (37 CFR § 2.68)
rubrics_metrics.description: During an ex parte appeal, the applicant may expressly abandon an application by filing a written request for abandonment or withdrawal signed by the applicant, someone with legal authority to bind the applicant, or a practitioner qualified to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as provided in § 2.135, express abandonment during an ex parte appeal shall not affect any rights that the applicant may have in the mark in the abandoned application for other Office proceedings. In contrast, after commencement of an opposition, concurrent use, or interference, abandonment without the written consent of every adverse party will result in judgment against the applicant. See 37 CFR § 2.193(e)(2) and TBMP §§ 602.01, 603.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of cancellation or assignment of cited registration on § 2(d) refusals
rubrics_metrics.description: If, during pendency of an ex parte appeal involving a refusal under Trademark Act § 2(d) (likelihood of confusion with a registered mark), the cited registration is cancelled or assigned to the applicant, the appeal will be moot insofar as that issue is concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the § 2(d) refusal based on that registration is the only issue in the appeal, the Board will dismiss the appeal as moot and the application will be sent to the examining attorney for approval for publication (or registration for a Supplemental Register application). If additional issues remain, the appeal proceeds on those issues. Applicants are recommended to periodically check the status of cited registrations and immediately notify the Board if a cited registration expires, is cancelled, or assigned. See TBMP § 1203.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of appeal on applicant request (good cause examples and monitoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to the Board's decision, proceedings may be suspended by the Board upon written request by the applicant showing good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples where suspension may be granted include: (1) the applicant is involved in a civil action or Board inter partes proceeding that may be dispositive of the issues, (2) another application involving the same issue is also on appeal, and (3) a cited registration is due for an affidavit of continued use or renewal. If suspension is requested based on possible cancellation for failure to file an affidavit, the Board will grant the request if it acts after the 5th anniversary of the registration's issue date; for possible expiration for failure to renew, the Board will grant if it acts after the 9th anniversary of the issue or renewal date. When proceedings are suspended, the applicant should monitor the cited registration monthly and notify the Board as soon as the applicant learns the registration has been cancelled, expired, or that the required document has been accepted. Upon such notice the Board will resume proceedings as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examining attorney-requested suspension/remand when grace period passed
rubrics_metrics.description: If, in a § 2(d) refusal situation, it comes to the examining attorney's attention that the grace period for filing an affidavit of continued use or renewal for the cited registration has passed and Office records do not indicate such a paper was submitted, the examining attorney may request remand so the application can be suspended pending final disposition of the cited registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board will issue an order suspending the appeal and remanding the case to the examining attorney. If the cited registration is cancelled or expires and that registration was the only basis for refusal, the examining attorney will approve the application for publication (or registration for Supplemental Register) and should notify the applicant. If the § 2(d) refusal is only one of the issues, the examining attorney should notify the Board that the refusal with respect to that registration has been withdrawn and the Board will resume proceedings on remaining issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board sua sponte suspension when affidavit/renewal due date coincides with assignment for decision
rubrics_metrics.description: When an ex parte appeal has been assigned to a judge for final decision, the case will be suspended if the due date for filing an affidavit or renewal for the cited registration falls on or before the date the case is assigned for decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The due date is the anniversary date of the registration and does not include the grace period. In this situation the applicant will be advised that the Board is suspending proceedings and will be given the opportunity to inform the Board if it wishes the Board to render a decision without waiting to determine whether the cited registration will be cancelled or expire. If the applicant wishes the Board to proceed, the cited registration will be treated as existing and valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension when application remanded for amendment/reconsideration/new ground/additional evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings in an ex parte appeal may be suspended if the application is remanded to the examining attorney for consideration of an amendment to the application, a request for reconsideration of a final action, assertion of a new ground of refusal, or submission of additional evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See TBMP §§ 1202.02, 1203.02(a), 1203.02(b), 1204, 1205, 1206.01, 1207.02, 1207.06, and 1209 for treatment of these circumstances and instructions regarding the six-month response clause, omission where appropriate, and how the appellant and examining attorney should proceed after remand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant has filed appeals in two or more copending applications and the cases involve common issues of law or fact, the Board may order consolidation of the appeals for purposes of briefing, oral hearing, and/or final decision, upon request by either party or on its own initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may also consider two or more cases in one opinion even if they have not been consolidated. Consolidated cases presented on the same brief should bear the serial number of each consolidated application and a copy of the brief should be submitted for each application. Parties may, however, file different briefs in each case if they so desire. See cited authorities and examples (e.g., In re Anderson; In re Country Music Association; In re America Online).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative positions by applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may, in appropriate cases, take alternative positions with respect to a refusal to register (for example: argue the mark is not merely descriptive, and alternatively claim acquired distinctiveness under § 2(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is the applicant’s responsibility to make clear that it is taking alternative positions. See TBMP §§ 309.03 and 311.02(b) for related guidance. Alternative positions mirror the ability of the examining attorney to refuse on alternative grounds; be explicit in presenting alternatives.
